architecture: DamonClient unifies local WS (ws_transport) and relay tunnel (ChannelWriter) behind a TextWriter trait; one Reconnect supervisor task owns the inbound pump, redial backoff (100ms to 5s), and pending drain. Responses route via a pending map keyed by u64 id; prompt results go through the event channel to preserve ordering. The E2E layer in src/relay.rs uses X25519 plus bidirectional AES-256-GCM with sequence-as-nonce.
clean: E2E handshake symmetry (relay.rs daemon_handshake 143-197 vs client_handshake 199-244): proof order client-first matches; client proof sha256(token||cpub||dpub), daemon proof sha256(token||dpub||cpub), both constant-time compared; both bail on e2e_error auth; both check was_contributory; from_shared(false) sends c2d and receives d2c mirroring daemon_side=true; both seq counters start at 0
examples/client.rs permission auto-approve payload matches daemon contract (runtime.rs:767 reads outcome.optionId; allow-once is a listed optionId)
request retry semantics: failed send removes pending entry; dropped oneshot on link death gives bounded 3-attempt resend; server error responses never retried
Reconnect supervisor swaps writer before announcing Connected (client.rs:512-520); backoff resets on successful redial
ws_transport: Ping/Pong/Binary skipped, Close/Err end the pump; full mpsc breaks the pump
wait_connected: correct deadline via timeout_at; supervisor-gone distinguished from timeout
ticketed_url: token only in Authorization header; single-use 60s ticket in URL by design (api.rs:303-322)
handle_frame: Updates lossy via try_send by design; malformed JSON and non-u64 ids ignored
No SSE or UTF-8 chunk-boundary exposure: tungstenite delivers complete validated UTF-8 text messages
coverage: src/relay.rs:60-260 (E2e, daemon_handshake, client_handshake, from_shared, encrypt/decrypt, proof/derive_key)

files.description: Embedder WS/JSON-RPC client: reconnect supervisor, pending routing, event channel, ticket exchange
Minimal usage example: connect, initialize, prompt, event loop
Comparison target: E2e handshake, tunnel, client_connect

findings.evidence: src/client.rs:585-600: let mut map = pending.lock().await; for (_, p) in map.drain() { let result = Err(json!({message: connection closed})); match p { Pending::Direct(tx) => { drop(tx); } Pending::ToEvents { session_id } => { let _ = event_tx.send(ClientEvent::PromptDone { session_id, result }).await; } } }
findings.fix: Collect drained entries into a Vec, drop the lock, then await event_tx.send; or make the ToEvents drain try_send-based.
findings.scenario: Event consumer is slow or paused and the 64-cap event channel fills; link drops; Reconnect.run blocks in drain_pending on event_tx.send().await while still holding the pending mutex; prompt() (client.rs:419) takes self.pending.lock().await with no wait_connected and no timeout, so it blocks forever. Same root cause: handle_frame blocking send for Request/PromptDone on a full channel freezes the frame pump, halting response routing and reconnect handling.
findings.title: drain_pending holds pending mutex across event channel send await, so prompt() can block forever

findings.evidence: src/client.rs:354-362: let resp = reqwest::Client::new().post(format!(url + /v1/ws_ticket)).bearer_auth(token).send().await.context(ws_ticket request failed)?;
findings.fix: Set connect_timeout/timeout on the reqwest client or wrap the ticket exchange in tokio::time::timeout.
findings.scenario: With a token set, DamonClient::connect POSTs /v1/ws_ticket; if the daemon or a reverse proxy accepts TCP but never responds, reqwest default (no total/read timeout) makes send().await wait forever and connect() never returns regardless of the reconnect supervisor. The relay path bounds its handshake at 15s (relay.rs:529-531) but this path has no bound.
findings.title: ticketed_url uses reqwest::Client::new() with no timeout, so connect() can hang indefinitely

findings.evidence: src/client.rs:469-471: fn ws_transport(ws: Ws) splits without any WebSocketConfig, versus src/relay.rs:513-516 client_connect setting max_message_size(Some(4 << 20)).
findings.fix: Use connect_async_with_config in connect()/redial with the same 4MiB cap as the tunnel path.
findings.scenario: On a tokenless or ws:// path, a compromised proxy delivers a single 64MiB Text frame; tungstenite default max_message_size buffers it all, amplifying client memory. The relay client (client_connect) explicitly caps at 4MiB for the same threat, so coverage is inconsistent.
findings.title: Local WS path lacks the max_message_size cap the relay path applies

notes: cargo check/test not run per audit-only read-only constraint.
examples/client.rs API usage fully checked against contract: permission payload, PromptDone error mapping, event-taken-before-prompt ordering all correct, no API misuse.
damon-relay binary-side frame protocol left to BinRelaySrv; only client-daemon symmetry verified.
summary: Audit of src/client.rs (1-596) and examples/client.rs against src/relay.rs daemon-side E2E handshake and tunnel. Proof order (client-first), auth-failure handling, seq init 0, and d2c/c2d direction mapping are exactly symmetric. No SSE parsing path exists (tungstenite handles frame boundaries and UTF-8). Three defects: drain_pending deadlock on full event channel (Medium), missing timeout in ticketed_url (Medium), missing max_message_size cap on local WS path (Low).
